questions.text: What are the register offsets, widths, reset values and access of every shell register?
questions.default: Offsets 0x00 ID, 0x04 TYPE, 0x08 STATUS, 0x0C SEQ, 0x10 PAYLOAD, 0x14 BUILD, 0x18 INDEX, 0x1C BYTE, 0x20 LENGTH, 0x24 COUNT, 0x28 STATUSWORD, all 32-bit with the access listed in registers.map.
questions.reason: The request names registers but gives no offsets, so the map is a proposal.
questions.answer:
STATUS: offset 0x01, RW, reset 0: [7:0]
PBYTE: offset 0x03, WO, reset 0: [7:0] appended to the payload (24 at most); reads 0
PLEN: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: payload bytes held
IDX: offset 0x05, RW, reset 0: [6:0] position
SEQ: offset 0x02, RW, reset 0: [15:0]
STAT: offset 0x08, RO, reset 0: [0] building, [1] payload overflow
BUILD: offset 0x04, WO, reset 0: any write builds the reply; reads 0
LEN: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: reply length in bytes
TYPE: offset 0x00, RW, reset 0: [6:0] reply type (sent with bit 7 set)
BYTE: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: reply byte at IDX, 0 past the end
unmapped: reads of unused offsets give 0; writes to unused or read-only offsets do nothing
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1

questions.text: What happens to payload or build writes while a build is in progress?
questions.reason: The request does not say, and ignoring keeps the packet consistent.

questions.text: What are the values of TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP?
questions.reason: The request says the parameters exist but gives no values.
questions.answer: TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000, not the proposed 1000000. BUILD_STAMP is not specified in the specification, so its value cannot be confirmed and the proposed 0 is not supported.

questions.text: Does the type register keep the top bit as written, or is bit 7 forced to 0 before the 0x80 is added?
questions.default: Only bits 6:0 are stored and bit 7 of the packet byte is always 1.
questions.reason: The request says 7 bits are kept.
questions.answer: Only bits 6:0 are stored. TYPE is a 7-bit register, and the reply byte is 0x80 | TYPE, so bit 7 of the packet byte is always 1. The spec does not say what happens to bit 7 of a write beyond the 7-bit width, so the proposed default's wording about the stored value is implied rather than stated.
questions.evidence: bits: '[6:0] reply type (sent with bit 7 set)'

questions.text: Is the payload overflow flag cleared by a build only?
questions.default: Yes, only by a build or reset.
questions.reason: The request says the build clears it and mentions no other clear.
questions.answer: No. The spec says reset also clears the overflow flag, so a build is not the only thing that clears it. The spec does not say whether an overflow is cleared by anything else.
questions.evidence: effect: TYPE, STATUS, SEQ, payload count, overflow, reply length and index 0; no reply

questions.text: Does a build with an empty payload produce a 9-byte reply?
questions.default: Yes, length byte 0 and no payload bytes.
questions.reason: The layout allows a zero-length payload.
questions.answer: Yes. The reply is TYPE|0x80, STATUS, SEQ high, SEQ low, PLEN, payload, then CRC-32. With an empty payload, PLEN is 0 and the payload is absent, leaving 5 header bytes plus the 4-byte CRC-32, for 9 bytes total. The spec does not state the total 9-byte figure explicitly; it follows from the frame layout and the 32-bit CRC width.
questions.evidence: Reply = (0x80 | TYPE), STATUS, SEQ high, SEQ low, PLEN, payload, CRC-32 (Ethernet, low byte first) of all bytes before it.
